newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close up led by Teva's sharp rise.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close up led by Teva's sharp rise.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher in selective and sluggish trading led by a sharp rise in Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 2.85 points, or 1.53 percent, to 189.62 on an all-share turnover of only 50 million shekels against 63 million on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 index rose 1.55 percent to 198.82.
This was the last day of trading before the Jewish New Year holiday. On Sunday there will be no trading because of the holiday.

"Trading was mixed and selective and all the activity was concentrated in a very few shares. Teva led the market and was the main contributor to its rise," said Eran Goren, managing director of Zannex Securities.

Teva, the most active share, surged 6.0 percent to 123,392 on volume of only 3.5 million shekels. Teva announced it had received approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to manufacture and market Clonazepam tablets, a generic equivalent of Roche's Klonpin, indicated for the treatment of seizure disorders.
Agis Industries surged 8.5 percent to 2,361 after Zannex Securities announced it had raised its recommendation for the share from "buy" to "strong buy".
"The market rose today but activity was very low and selective. The mood improved because of Teva's rise and the weakening of the shekel against the dollar during the last few days," said one dealer.
"The market also rose because of Wednesday's gains by Israeli shares traded on Nasdaq," he added.
Other active shares include Koor Industries, which gained 1.0 percent to 27,677 on turnover of 2.5 million shekels and Tadiran, which rose 3.25 percent to 1,399 on volume of 2.1 million shekels.
